references.text: Jacob's blessing of Judah specifically, which prophesies leadership and kingship from his line—a prophecy that springs forth from Judah's birth in Genesis 29:35.
The context for Judah's birth: Leah had already borne three sons and experienced the Lord seeing her misery. With Judah, she moves from seeking a husband's love to praising the Lord.
An encouragement to give the Lord glory and praise, reflecting Leah's declaration: 'This time I will praise the Lord' (אוֹדֶה אֶת־יְהוָה).
'Judah is my scepter'—God appoints Judah to a leadership role, reflecting the special position his tribe would hold.
Jesus's genealogy shows that He is of Judah's line through Judah, son of Jacob—in accordance with prophecies about the Messiah.
Jesus's genealogy through Luke, which includes Judah and confirms Jesus's belonging to the tribe of Judah.
Jesus is referred to as 'the Lion of the tribe of Judah' who has conquered—the ultimate fulfillment of the promises connected to Judah.
The book of Hebrews confirms that Jesus descends from the tribe of Judah, linking back to Judah's birth and God's plan.
A contrast between Leah's praise of God's grace and the prophet's declaration of judgment that mercy will cease.
A parallel between Leah and Hannah: both bear sons in answer to prayer and as a sign that God has removed their shame.
